chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Musa ibn Ja'far from Wahb al-Baghdadi from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'If you shun the great sins which you are forbidden, We will do away with your small [sins]'
He (peace be upon him) replied: 'One who keeps away from that for which Allah has threatened with the Fire, if he is a believer, Allah will forgive his sins and make him enter a noble place.'

And the seven greater sins that are obligatory [to avoid] are: killing the innocent soul, disobedience to parents, consuming usury, apostasy after migration, accusing a chaste woman, consuming the property of an orphan, and fleeing from the battle.

key_terms.أَکْلُ مَالِ الْیَتِیمِ: Consuming the property of the orphan

ai.seo_question: What are the seven major sins that lead to Hellfire according to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the conditional nature of Quran 4:31, specifying that the expiation of minor sins is contingent upon the believer's avoidance of the seven decisive major sins (al-Kaba'ir al-Mubiqat). This narration, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, provides a definitive list including the killing of the innocent, disobedience to parents, and consuming usury, thereby linking theological promise to specific ethical obligations in Shia jurisprudence.
